title: SplashBI Opens Hyderabad GCC, Plans $100 Million Investment Over Five to Seven Years
headline: SplashBI Opens Hyderabad GCC, Plans $100 Million Investment Over Five to Seven Years
subheadline: The 20,000-square-foot Financial District centre seats 275 professionals and will build the US company's data platform and SplashAI capabilities. A further $4 million is earmarked for an AI data centre.
summary: The 20,000-square-foot Financial District centre seats 275 professionals and will build the US company's data platform and SplashAI capabilities. A further $4 million is earmarked for an AI data centre.
excerpt: The 20,000-square-foot Financial District centre seats 275 professionals and will build the US company's data platform and SplashAI capabilities. A further $4 million is earmarked for an AI data centre.
body:
• SplashBI, a Georgia, US-headquartered enterprise data intelligence company, has opened a 20,000-square-foot Global Capability Centre at VSD Tech Park in Hyderabad's Financial District, with capacity for 275 professionals.
  • The company plans to invest more than $100 million over the next five to seven years in infrastructure, technology and talent, and has separately earmarked $4 million for an AI data centre.
  • Telangana IT Minister D. Sridhar Babu inaugurated the centre. SplashBI has operated in Hyderabad since 2014 and serves more than 500 enterprise customers across 39 countries.

SplashBI, the Georgia-headquartered enterprise data intelligence platform, opened its Global Capability Centre in Hyderabad on Monday and said it will invest more than $100 million over the next five to seven years to scale the centre.

The 20,000-square-foot facility at VSD Tech Park in the Financial District can house 275 professionals and was inaugurated by D. Sridhar Babu, Telangana's Minister for IT, Electronics and Communications, Industries and Commerce, according to the company's announcement. The company has also earmarked $4 million for an AI data centre to strengthen its AI infrastructure, Express Computer reported.

What the centre will do

The Hyderabad GCC will work on platform engineering, AI development, data science, domain analytics and global customer delivery. In practical terms, its teams will build the data connectivity and business modelling behind SplashBI's platform, develop its SplashAI capabilities, and support customer implementations — the work of helping enterprises connect business data scattered across functions and use it for decisions, AI, analytics and reporting.

SplashBI has had a presence in Hyderabad since 2014; the new facility brings its city teams together under one roof. Globally, the company says it has a workforce of about 400 and serves more than 500 enterprise organisations across 39 countries.

"Enterprises need a practical way to turn the data they already have into decisions they can trust."

— Naveen Miglani, CEO and Co-Founder, SplashBI

Why Hyderabad keeps winning these centres

Miglani said the Hyderabad centre strengthens the engineering and customer expertise behind that work, as customers advance their data foundations and adopt AI with the right business context. President and Co-Founder Kiran Reddy Pasham said the Hyderabad teams will build the platform capabilities and domain content that help customers connect their data and use it in everyday work.

The opening is the latest in a steady run of US-headquartered firms placing global capability centres in Hyderabad's Financial District corridor, drawn by the city's engineering talent base. For Hyderabad's tech workforce, the centre's 275 roles sit in platform engineering and AI — the higher-value end of GCC hiring — rather than back-office support.

What to watch

The $100 million figure is a plan spread over five to seven years, not money already spent; the pace of hiring toward the 275-seat capacity and the build-out of the $4 million AI data centre will show how quickly the plan becomes headcount.
